newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toshiba to invest 100 bln yen for new LSI chips.
newsitem.headline: Toshiba to invest 100 bln yen for new LSI chips.

text.p: Toshiba Corp said on Thursday that it would invest a total of 100 billion yen to renovate its plant in Oita, southern Kyushu, for the production of next-generation system large-scale integration (LSI) chips.
The 100 billion yen investment will be made over several years, a company spokesman said.

The plant, which will adopt 0.25 micron technology, will start mass production of 0.25 micron system LSI chips in the second half of the 1997/98 business year ending March 31, the Toshiba spokesman said.
Output is expected to be 100,000 chips per month initially, rising to one million chips in calendar 2000, he said.
The plant may adopt more advanced 0.18 micron technology in the future, he said.
Toshiba's Oita plant now produces 16-megabit dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips and 0.35 micron system LSIs, the company spokesman said.
System LSI is a "system on a chip" which has various components, such as a DRAM and micro processing unit (MPU), in one chip. It is mainly used for workstations at the moment.

The 0.25 micron system LSI chips that Toshiba plans to produce in Oita will have a 64-megabit DRAM and a 32-bit MPU, the Toshiba spokesman said. Depending on users' demand, they may also have integrated circuits for three-dimensional image processing, he said.
